passages.text: “But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
passages.sermon: Job, listen to me now.\r\nHear my words.\r\nPay attention to everything I say.
passages.original: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע־ נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל־ דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה׃

passages.text: Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.
passages.sermon:
Elihu is speaking to Job.
Elihu is about to speak.
I open my mouth now.
My tongue is ready to speak.
My words are about to come out.
passages.original: הִנֵּה־ נָ֭א פָּתַ֣חְתִּי פִ֑י דִּבְּרָ֖ה לְשׁוֹנִ֣י בְחִכִּֽי׃

passages.text: My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.
passages.sermon:
I speak now.
My heart is upright.
My words come from this upright heart.
I speak what I know.
My lips speak with sincerity.
My words are clear and honest.
passages.original: יֹֽשֶׁר־ לִבִּ֥י אֲמָרָ֑י וְדַ֥עַת שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י בָּר֥וּר מִלֵּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
passages.sermon:
God created me.
God used His Spirit to make me.
The Almighty gave me life.
His breath keeps me alive.
passages.original: רֽוּחַ־ אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: Refute me if you can; prepare your case and confront me.
passages.sermon:
I am speaking to you now.
You may try to answer me if you are able.
Set your words in order before me.
Stand up and present your case to me.
passages.original: אִם־ תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה׃

passages.text: I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay.
passages.sermon:
I am a human being like you.
God made me from clay.
I stand before God just as you do.
I am not different from you in this way.
We both come from the same material.
passages.original: הֵן־ אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם־ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
passages.sermon:
I will not make you afraid.
You do not need to fear me.
I will not treat you harshly.
My hand will not be heavy on you.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֭מָתִי לֹ֣א תְבַעֲתֶ֑ךָּ וְ֝אַכְפִּ֗י עָלֶ֥יךָ לֹא־ יִכְבָּֽד׃

passages.text: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard these very words: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, with no iniquity in me.
passages.sermon:
You spoke these words where I could hear them.
I listened to your very words.
You said, “I am pure.
I have no transgression.
I am clean.
There is no iniquity in me.”
passages.original: אַ֭ךְ אָמַ֣רְתָּ בְאָזְנָ֑י וְק֖וֹל מִלִּ֣ין אֶשְׁמָֽע׃ זַ֥ךְ אֲנִ֗י בְּֽלִ֫י פָ֥שַׁע חַ֥ף אָנֹכִ֑י וְלֹ֖א עָוֺ֣ן לִֽי׃

passages.text: Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.
passages.sermon: God looks for reasons to accuse me.\r\nGod treats me as His enemy.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן תְּ֭נוּאוֹת עָלַ֣י יִמְצָ֑א יַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’
passages.sermon:
God puts my feet in the stocks.
God restrains me.
God watches all my paths.
God observes everything I do.
God pays close attention to my ways.
passages.original: יָשֵׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֣ד רַגְלָ֑י יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כָּל־ אָרְחֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: Behold, you are not right in this matter. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
passages.sermon: You are not right in this matter.\r\nI will answer you.\r\nGod is greater than man.
passages.original: הֶן־ זֹ֣את לֹא־ צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־ יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?
passages.sermon:
God is greater than man.
You complain to God.
You say God does not answer you.
You say God does not reply to any of your words.
You ask why God does not respond to your questions.
passages.original: מַ֭דּוּעַ אֵלָ֣יו רִיב֑וֹתָ כִּ֥י כָל־ דְּ֝בָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א־ יַעֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.
passages.sermon:
God is greater than man.
God speaks to people in one way.
God also speaks in another way.
People do not notice when God speaks.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ בְאַחַ֥ת יְדַבֶּר־ אֵ֑ל וּ֝בִשְׁתַּ֗יִם לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds, He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride, to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to people in many ways.
God sometimes speaks in dreams.
God sometimes speaks in visions at night.
People sleep deeply on their beds.
God opens their ears while they sleep.
God warns them with strong messages.
God warns people to turn them away from wrongdoing.
God warns people to keep them from pride.
God wants to save a person’s soul from the Pit.
God wants to keep a person’s life from dying by the sword.
passages.original: בַּחֲל֤וֹם׀ חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֣ל תַּ֭רְדֵּמָה עַל־ אֲנָשִׁ֑ים בִּ֝תְנוּמ֗וֹת עֲלֵ֣י מִשְׁכָּֽב׃ אָ֣ז יִ֭גְלֶה אֹ֣זֶן אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּבְמֹ֖סָרָ֣ם יַחְתֹּֽם׃ לְ֭הָסִיר אָדָ֣ם מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְגֵוָ֖ה מִגֶּ֣בֶר יְכַסֶּֽה׃ יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־ שָׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ מֵעֲבֹ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁלַח׃

passages.text: A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones, so that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.
passages.sermon:
God sometimes corrects a man.
God uses pain to do this.
The man lies on his bed.
He feels pain in his body.
His bones hurt all the time.
He no longer wants to eat bread.
He hates the food he once loved.
His soul turns away from his favorite food.
passages.original: וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל־ מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ וְרִיב עֲצָמָ֣יו אֵתָֽן׃ וְזִֽהֲמַ֣תּוּ חַיָּת֣וֹ לָ֑חֶם וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מַאֲכַ֥ל תַּאֲוָֽה׃

passages.text: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his hidden bones protrude.
passages.sermon:
A man suffers greatly.
His body becomes weak.
His flesh wastes away.
People can no longer see his healthy form.
His bones, once hidden, now stick out.
His body shows clear signs of sickness.
passages.original: יִ֣כֶל בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מֵרֹ֑אִי וּשְׁפִי עַ֝צְמוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א רֻאּֽוּ׃

passages.text: He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
passages.sermon:
This man suffers greatly.
\r\nHe becomes very weak.
\r\nHe comes close to death.
\r\nHis soul approaches the grave.
\r\nHis life nears the messengers of death.
passages.original: וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים׃

passages.text: Yet if there is a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him, to be gracious to him and say, ‘Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom,’ then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.
passages.sermon:
A man suffers and draws near to death.
If there is a messenger for him, this messenger stands on his side.
This messenger is a mediator.
He is one among a thousand.
The messenger tells the man what is right for him.
The messenger shows grace to the man.
The messenger says, “Spare him from going down to the Pit.
I have found a ransom for him.”
Then the man’s flesh becomes fresh like a child’s.
He returns to the days of his youth.
passages.original: אִם־ יֵ֤שׁ עָלָ֨יו׀ מַלְאָ֗ךְ מֵלִ֗יץ אֶחָ֥ד מִנִּי־ אָ֑לֶף לְהַגִּ֖יד לְאָדָ֣ם יָשְׁרֽוֹ׃ וַיְחֻנֶּ֗נּוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּ֭דָעֵהוּ מֵרֶ֥דֶת שָׁ֗חַת מָצָ֥אתִי כֹֽפֶר׃ רֻֽטֲפַ֣שׁ בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מִנֹּ֑עַר יָ֝שׁ֗וּב לִימֵ֥י עֲלוּמָֽיו׃

passages.text: He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God’s face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man.
passages.sermon:
A man prays to God.
God accepts him.
The man sees God's face.
The man shouts with joy.
God restores righteousness to the man.
passages.original: יֶעְתַּ֤ר אֶל־ אֱל֨וֹהַּ׀ וַיִּרְצֵ֗הוּ וַיַּ֣רְא פָּ֭נָיו בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׁב לֶ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ צִדְקָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then he sings before men with these words: ‘I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved.
passages.sermon:
A man stands before other people.
He speaks openly to them.
He says, “I have sinned.
I have twisted what is right.
I did not receive what I deserved.”
passages.original: יָשֹׁ֤ר׀ עַל־ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָ֭טָאתִי וְיָשָׁ֥ר הֶעֱוֵ֗יתִי וְלֹא־ שָׁ֥וָה לִֽי׃

passages.text: He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.’
passages.sermon:
God redeemed my soul.
He saved me from going down to the Pit.
I will live.
I will see the light.
passages.original: פָּדָ֣ה נַפְשִׁי מֵעֲבֹ֣ר בַּשָּׁ֑חַת וְחַיָּתִי בָּא֥וֹר תִּרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: Behold, all these things God does to a man, two or even three times, to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
passages.sermon:
God acts in these ways toward a person.
God does this two or even three times.
God does this to bring back a person’s soul from the Pit.
God does this so the person may see the light of life.
passages.original: הֶן־ כָּל־ אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל־ אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם־ גָּֽבֶר׃ לְהָשִׁ֣יב נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־ שָׁ֑חַת לֵ֝א֗וֹר בְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַיִּים׃

passages.text: Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
passages.sermon:
Elihu spoke to Job.
Elihu said, "Job, pay attention."
Listen to me.
Be silent.
I will speak.
passages.original: הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע־ לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.
passages.sermon:
Elihu spoke to Job.
Elihu wanted to help Job.
Elihu said, “If you have something to say, answer me.
Speak up.
I want to show that you are right.”
passages.original: אִם־ יֵשׁ־ מִלִּ֥ין הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי דַּ֝בֵּ֗ר כִּֽי־ חָפַ֥צְתִּי צַדְּקֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: But if not, then listen to me; be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.”
passages.sermon:
Elihu spoke to Job.
Elihu was a young man.
Elihu wanted to teach Job.
Elihu said, “If you have nothing to say, listen to me.
Be silent.
I will teach you wisdom.”
passages.original: אִם־ אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע־ לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה׃ס
